items:
A work permit must be issued and the qualified
maintenance staff should carry the suitable safety category,

The circuit breaker must be isolated completely and
properly earthed from both sides,

Safety fence (rope) with caution marks surrounding the
work area.

Isolate the DC voltage for the
earthing switch,

Wear safety helmet, shoes, breathing mask, safety
glasses.
DC control power should be disconnected.

Before using a blower to clean the control cabinet or
when cleaning the insulators, wear breathing mask to protect your lung tissues
from the dust particles.

Don't burn the cloth used in cleaning, collect it and
send it to the dump.
Safety helmet, shoes, breathing mask, safety glasses.
Safety fence (rope) with caution marks.

Hydraulic test gauges, hydraulic oil, and SF6 gas if
needed,
SF6 test gauge, micro ohmmeter, and Air Blower,

Dew point equipment, acidity equipment, Air content
equipment, and timing equipment
Check the high voltage terminals.
Visual check and cleaning the insulators.
Measure the humidity of the SF6 gas (Dew point).

Check the tightness of the compressed air pipe work and
couplings.
Check the terminals in the control cubical.
Visual Check of the control cubicle.
Check holding down bolts of the base.
Check the paint finish.

Substations | Technical Procedure
Introduction
This
procedure details the majormaintenance
procedure P1for the circuit breaker,
which should be carried out five years or after 2000 operation, as indicated by
Y5 in the above title block.
The first draft document initiated by Cairo
zone.
Safety Precautions
A work permit must be issued and the qualified
maintenance staff should carry the suitable safety category,
The circuit breaker must be isolated completely and
properly earthed from both sides,
Safety fence (rope) with caution marks surrounding the
work area.
Isolate the DC voltage for the
earthing switch,
Wear safety helmet, shoes, breathing mask, safety
glasses.
DC control power should be disconnected.
Before using a blower to clean the control cabinet or
when cleaning the insulators, wear breathing mask to protect your lung tissues
from the dust particles.
Don't burn the cloth used in cleaning, collect it and
send it to the dump.
Tools and
Equipment
Safety helmet, shoes, breathing mask, safety glasses.
Safety fence (rope) with caution marks.
Hydraulic test gauges, hydraulic oil, and SF6 gas if
needed,
SF6 test gauge, micro ohmmeter, and Air Blower,
Dew point equipment, acidity equipment, Air content
equipment, and timing equipment
Check the high voltage terminals.
Visual check and cleaning the insulators.

Check the tightness of the compressed air pipe work and
couplings.
Check the terminals in the control cubical.
